answer:
**A calibration plot compares promised frequency with observed frequency.** Group examples with similar predicted probabilities. If 1000 examples average 0.20 but only 100 are positive, that bin has a 0.10 probability gap. ECE averages absolute bin gaps weighted by bin size. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html) [2](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html)

Brier score instead averages $(p-y)^2$ per example. Predicting 0.9 for a positive incurs 0.01; predicting 0.9 for a negative incurs 0.81. It evaluates probability quality without choosing bins, though its decomposition includes more than calibration alone.

**Normalized cross-entropy supplies a baseline comparison.** Under the convention used here, divide model log loss by the log loss of a constant predictor using the reference prevalence. If baseline loss is 0.20 and model loss is 0.15, NE=0.75: the model has 25% lower loss under that baseline definition. Other naming conventions exist, so state yours.

ECE can hide errors inside wide bins or opposing subgroup errors. Log loss strongly penalizes confidently wrong predictions. Evaluate reliability curves, slices, ranking, and online utility together. Published use of a metric does not establish a company's universal current “north-star” metric; the mathematical reason to use normalized loss is its reference to a specified baseline, not an appeal to a company name.

**Technical details and references.**

ECE bins predicted probabilities and averages absolute confidence-versus-frequency gaps, weighted by bin size. Brier score is mean squared probability error. Normalized cross-entropy divides model log loss by a specified baseline entropy/log loss. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html) [2](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html)

$$ECE=\sum_b\frac{n_b}{N}|acc_b-conf_b|,\quad BS=N^{-1}\sum_i(p_i-y_i)^2,\quad NE=\frac{logloss}{-\pi\log\pi-(1-\pi)\log(1-\pi)}.$$

For this NE convention, values below one beat the constant-prevalence predictor. State the convention because names vary. ECE depends on binning and can hide subgroup errors. Log loss strongly penalizes confident mistakes and is useful for ads probabilities, but no unsupported claim about a company's universal current “north-star” metric is needed. Report ranking, calibration, and online utility together.
